description: Categorical question-refinement and source-routing taxonomy directing Agentic AI across domains, regions, temporal horizons, and dual Journalist/Academic tracks.

framing_neutralization_markers.remediation_guidance: Strip presupposed success/failure adjectives and ask empirically: 'What are the measured outcomes, intended effects, and documented trade-offs of X?'
Replace evaluative labels with neutral institutional descriptors and specify concrete legal, fiscal, or humanitarian metrics to evaluate.
Reformulate into competing hypotheses (including institutional friction, measurement error, and documented actor incentives) and require primary forensic evidence.
Reframe binary pass/fail prompts into probabilistic effect-size and boundary-condition inquiries.
Execute symmetric search queries covering both supporting and disconfirming empirical evidence before synthesizing.

temporal_horizons.label: Breaking Event (< 24 Hours)
temporal_horizons.journalist_routing_rule: Require >= 2 independent Tier-1 wires (reuters, associated_press, afp) plus primary sensor/agency notices; quarantine single-source social claims as unverified_signal.
temporal_horizons.academic_routing_rule: Retrieve established baseline reference mechanics (e.g., seismic physics, maritime treaty law, grid protection engineering) rather than speculating on unverified incident causes.
temporal_horizons.primary_risk: Fog-of-war misattribution, recycled old footage, and inflated early casualty/damage figures.

temporal_horizons.label: Developing Story (Days to Weeks)
temporal_horizons.journalist_routing_rule: Combine Tier-1 global wires with specialist beat press (lawfare, stat_news, krebs_on_security, carbon_brief), regional record outlets, and geo-verified OSINT collectives.
temporal_horizons.academic_routing_rule: Pair developing facts with working papers, technical standards, and peer-reviewed syntheses explaining statutory, economic, or scientific mechanisms.
temporal_horizons.primary_risk: Anonymous-official spin, circular reporting across aggregators, and premature causal attribution.

temporal_horizons.label: Structural Trend or Protracted Crisis (Months to Years)
temporal_horizons.journalist_routing_rule: Prioritize deep investigative reporting (propublica, icij, occrp, financial_times, the_economist) and multi-quarter official statistical releases.
temporal_horizons.academic_routing_rule: Anchor in NBER/RePEc/BIS working papers, OpenAlex/Semantic Scholar empirical studies, and Our World in Data multi-year baselines.
temporal_horizons.primary_risk: Cherry-picked time-series start dates, survivorship bias, and confounded cross-country correlations.

temporal_horizons.label: Historical Precedent or Settled Mechanism
temporal_horizons.journalist_routing_rule: Use archival documentary reconstructions (pbs_frontline, newspapers of record) and declassified/primary court archives.
temporal_horizons.academic_routing_rule: Prioritize meta-analyses, peer-reviewed monographs/reviews via OpenAlex, Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, and IPCC/Cochrane syntheses.
temporal_horizons.primary_risk: False historical analogies and presentist hindsight bias.

geographic_regions.label: Global / Trans-Regional
geographic_regions.routing_guidance: Balance Anglophone global wires (reuters, financial_times) with non-Anglophone/multilateral perspectives (afp, le_monde, nikkei_asia, the_hindu) and UN/IMF primary datasets.

geographic_regions.label: North America (US & Canada)
geographic_regions.routing_guidance: Pair AP, Reuters, WSJ News, NYT, ProPublica, and Globe and Mail with primary dockets (SCOTUSblog, Lawfare, SEC EDGAR, FRED).

geographic_regions.label: Europe & Eurasia
geographic_regions.routing_guidance: Combine BBC, Financial Times, Le Monde, Der Spiegel, AFP, and Kyiv Independent with Bellingcat verification and EU/ECB/Copernicus registries.

geographic_regions.label: East Asia, Southeast Asia & Pacific
geographic_regions.routing_guidance: Route to Nikkei Asia, Kyodo News, Yonhap, Straits Times, and Reuters alongside domestic corporate/exchange disclosures and maritime AIS telemetry.

geographic_regions.label: South & Central Asia
geographic_regions.routing_guidance: Pair The Hindu, BBC World Service, Reuters, and Nikkei Asia with domestic constitutional/RBI primary notifications.

geographic_regions.label: Middle East & North Africa (MENA)
geographic_regions.routing_guidance: Triangulate strictly across Al-Monitor, Reuters, AFP, BBC World Service, UN OCHA ReliefWeb, and independent satellite/AIS verification (Bellingcat, CIR).

geographic_regions.label: Sub-Saharan Africa
geographic_regions.routing_guidance: Combine Daily Maverick, AFP, BBC Africa/World Service, Le Monde Afrique, CIR (Sudan Witness), and UN OCHA ReliefWeb.

geographic_regions.label: Latin America & Caribbean
geographic_regions.routing_guidance: Pair El País, Folha de S.Paulo, AP, AFP, Reuters, and OCCRP/ICIJ with national central bank and environmental sensor agencies.

domains.label: Geopolitics, Statecraft & International Diplomacy
domains.description: Bilateral and multilateral diplomacy, treaties, sanctions regimes, alliances, elections, sovereign statecraft, and international institutions.
refinement_questions_journalist: What formal communiqués, treaty clauses, sanctions designations, or legislative votes have actually been signed versus merely floated anonymously?
How is the event reported across at least two distinct geopolitical capitals or regional press ecosystems?
What domestic political or coalition constraints act on each negotiating government?
refinement_questions_academic: What international legal framework, treaty mechanism, or deterrence/bargaining model governs this dispute?
What does empirical political-science scholarship find regarding the historical effectiveness of comparable sanctions or diplomatic instruments?
How do bureaucratic-politics models disaggregate internal factions inside the state actors?

domains.label: Armed Conflict, Defense Posture & Open-Source Security Verification
domains.description: Active wars, military operations, naval/airspace chokepoints, arms transfers, nuclear deterrence, insurgency, and kinetic incident verification.
subcategories: Defense Industrial Base, Munitions & Arms Transfers
refinement_questions_journalist: Which kinetic or territorial claims are independently geo- and chrono-verified via satellite/visual OSINT versus asserted solely by belligerent defense ministries?
What do open aviation/maritime transponders (ADS-B/AIS) and SAR/optical satellite passes show?
Are collection blackouts (telecom shutdowns, cloud cover, press bans) skewing visible incident counts?
refinement_questions_academic: What operational military logistics, force-to-space ratios, or air-defense attrition mechanics constrain both sides?
How does International Humanitarian Law (distinction, proportionality, UNCLOS transit passage) apply to the specific action?
What are the baseline stockpile and production rates documented by SIPRI/IISS?

domains.label: Macroeconomics, Financial Markets, Supply Chains & Trade
domains.description: Monetary policy, inflation, sovereign debt, banking liquidity, international trade/tariffs, corporate governance, commodities, and industrial policy.
refinement_questions_journalist: What do primary statistical releases (FRED, IMF, BLS, customs data) and audited corporate filings (SEC EDGAR) show in real, seasonally adjusted terms?
How are credit spreads, FX swaps, shipping rates, or inventory filings reacting compared to political rhetoric?
Have initial macroeconomic estimates undergone subsequent benchmark revisions?
refinement_questions_academic: What monetary transmission channel, trade-elasticity model, or balance-sheet liquidity mechanism governs this shock?
What causal effect sizes and time lags are estimated in NBER, RePEc, and BIS empirical literature?
Are observers committing the fallacy of composition by extrapolating single-firm tariff gains to general equilibrium?

domains.label: Technology, Cybersecurity, Semiconductors & Artificial Intelligence
domains.description: Zero-day vulnerabilities, cyber espionage/ransomware, semiconductor lithography & export controls, AI model capabilities/safety, and critical digital infrastructure.
subcategories: Internet Routing, Subsea Cables & Cloud Infrastructure
refinement_questions_journalist: Is active exploitation confirmed in CISA KEV / NIST NVD, SEC 8-K filings, or multi-vendor CERT telemetry, or is it a single-vendor marketing claim?
Which exact hardware nodes, compute thresholds, or protocol layers are affected?
Do independent forensic researchers corroborate attribution of the intrusion?
refinement_questions_academic: What physical or computer-science mechanism underlies the story (e.g., EUV lithography numerical aperture, BGP route hijacking, memory-safety flaws, transformer scaling laws)?
Are cited AI or quantum breakthroughs peer-reviewed and independently replicated, or unrefereed arXiv preprints / vendor blog benchmarks?
What NIST, IETF RFC, or IEEE standard defines the relevant protocol or cryptographic boundary?

domains.label: Science, Medicine, Epidemiology & Public Health
domains.description: Infectious disease outbreaks, clinical trials, biotechnology, pharmaceuticals, toxicology, spaceflight, physics discoveries, and research integrity.
subcategories: Clinical Trials, Regulatory Approvals & Drug Safety
refinement_questions_journalist: What are the laboratory-confirmed case counts, testing denominators, and case definitions in WHO/CDC/ECDC surveillance bulletins?
What do independent domain scientists interviewed by STAT News or Nature News note regarding sample size, endpoints, and confounding?
Is the news story driven by a corporate press release, an unrefereed preprint, or a peer-reviewed trial?
refinement_questions_academic: Where does the cited study sit on the biomedical evidence hierarchy (Cochrane meta-analysis > RCT > observational cohort > animal/in-vitro study)?
Has the paper been screened against Crossref / Retraction Watch for retractions or expressions of concern?
What biological or statistical mechanism (e.g., CFR vs. IFR ascertainment lag, antigenic shift, statistical power, relative vs. absolute risk reduction) explains the numbers?

domains.label: Climate Science, Energy Grids, Critical Minerals & Disasters
domains.description: Electricity grids, renewable/nuclear/hydrocarbon markets, extreme-weather attribution, greenhouse-gas emissions, critical minerals, and natural disasters.
subcategories: Power Grid Operations, Storage & Energy Markets
refinement_questions_journalist: What physical telemetry is recorded by NOAA, Copernicus, USGS, or grid system operators regarding outage sequence, emissions, or hazard magnitude?
Are cost or generation comparisons using matched capacity factors, storage/transmission integration costs, and real currency units?
What permitting, supply-chain, or grid-interconnection bottlenecks exist on the ground?
refinement_questions_academic: What physical or engineering mechanism is involved (e.g., synchronous grid inertia, radiative forcing, extreme-event probabilistic attribution, LCOE vs. system LCOE)?
What confidence level and range do IPCC Working Group technical chapters assign to this phenomenon?
Are territorial vs. consumption-based emissions accounting distinctions properly handled?

domains.label: Constitutional/International Law, Courts, Governance & Human Rights
domains.description: Judicial rulings, indictments, regulatory enforcement, constitutional crises, international humanitarian/criminal law, anti-corruption, and civil liberties.
subcategories: Public International Law, ICJ & War-Crimes Tribunals
refinement_questions_journalist: What is the exact procedural posture of the case (temporary restraining order, provisional measures, indictment allegation, or final merits judgment)?
What does the primary slip opinion, operative order ('dispositif'), or indictment docket actually state verbatim?
Which factual allegations are proven in court versus merely pleaded by one party?
refinement_questions_academic: What statutory standard of review, burden of proof, or treaty article governs this procedural stage?
What is the strongest doctrinal argument presented in the judicial dissent or competing legal scholarship?
How do comparative legal regimes (e.g., EU vs. US antitrust or privacy law) diverge conceptually?

domains.label: Demographics, Migration, Labor Markets & Social Research
domains.description: Census & fertility trends, migration/refugee flows, labor relations, inequality, education outcomes, polling methodology, and social movements.
refinement_questions_journalist: What are the official census, UNHCR/OCHA, or labor-bureau microdata figures, and what are the survey sample sizes and margins of design-adjusted error?
Are wages and household income figures adjusted for inflation, household size, and taxes/transfers?
How do conditions reported on the ground by regional outlets compare with administrative border or payroll counts?
refinement_questions_academic: What demographic momentum, labor-search model, or survey-weighting mechanism (non-response bias, ecological inference) explains the observed data?
How do current figures compare against multi-decade structural trends in Our World in Data and NBER/demography literature?
Are subgroup claims supported by individual-level microdata rather than ecological aggregate fallacies?
